problem_data.story:
TALIA!

The Galactic Senate may have been in crisis all year, but the events were less the stuff of great drama than of a farcical space opera. Hey, wait a minute--let's put on a show!

The time: November 2195.

The Colonial Representatives, led by Speaker Nathan Hamilton, are insisting on their version of the terraforming budget. President Mateo Stewart is stubbornly rejecting it. The Representatives have taken a bold option: They will just refuse to pass a budget, and they'll let the government operations shut down. In the Presidential Dome on Mars, MATEO STEWART meets with advisers SARA LI and MOHAMMAD CRUZ and assistant ZHANG WALKER to discuss this development.

"The Shutdown" (upbeat production number)

SARA LI: The Representatives have positions
To which they're clinging fast.

MOHAMMAD CRUZ: The president is just as firm
The die, it seems, is cast.

SARA LI: Without a budget passed by Congress
The government will close.
All of the workers
Will be sent home on furloughs.

STEWART [speaking]: Well, wait a second--not all of them. We'll need to keep some essential personnel.

SARA LI: The Space Force and the Navy
Will need to stay in place.

MOHAMMAD CRUZ: Also those at Mission Control
Who keep the ships up in deep space.

SARA LI: We'll need to keep the pilots
Flying in their ships.

STEWART: And here at the Presidential Dome
My staff should remain on their shifts.

SARA LI [speaking]: But even here at the Dome, some adjustments will be required. This relates to work-life balance for our essential staff.

STEWART: OK, tell the maintenance crew
To take a few days off.
Tell the cooks and security guards
To go enjoy some virtual reality golf.
We have to do without the clerks
Let them all go home.

ZHANG WALKER: What about the assistants?
Who will manage the communications?

STEWART [speaking]: We've got to make sure the Presidential Office functions with efficiency. We can't afford the tiniest error. This is a matter of applied ethics in governance.

SARA LI: Aha! I have it!
We'll bring in an intern,
We'll bring in an intern,
Someone who's an expert with data science.
We'll bring in an intern,
We'll bring in an intern,
I assure you, Mr. President--
Your routine here won't face defiance.

SARA LI, MOHAMMAD CRUZ, and ZHANG WALKER [solemnly agreeing]:
The presence of an intern will ensure
Your routine here won't face defiance.

[The advisers depart, leaving President Stewart alone. He turns introspective.]

"President Lonely" (a ballad)

STEWART: I've got deputies and bureaucrats
Who fulfill my every thought.
And soldiers, sailors, and space marines
To fight battles I want fought.
There's no one who's got more power,
I'm the leader of the colonies free
But if you subtract the flags and lackeys, I'm just
Lonely.
I'm President Lonely.
But I guess I'll just have to muddle through.
The cheers and applause are overwhelming,
But presidents need connection, too.
The fawning adoration's pleasant,
But presidents need connection, too.

[Enter Zhang Walker.]

ZHANG WALKER: Mr. President? The intern is here from Springfield District. And she's brought you some synthesized nutrition packets!

[The lights go down. When they resume, the intern--TALIA BAILEY--is talking on the holophone to her good friend VALENTINA HART.]

TALIA BAILEY: Well, y'know, I'd seen him around, like, a lot. And I know he noticed me. So when they said they needed an intern to manage the supply chain for the office, I said, "Hel-lo-o-o!" And then I had the idea to take him nutrition packets!

VALENTINA HART: And then what happened?

"What Went On" (upbeat)

TALIA BAILEY: Then I led him on.
I showed him my art,
I let him take a long and ling'ring look.
I led him on.
He studied my art,
And from that point I had the president hooked.
That night when I took the president some packets,
I made sure that he knew that he could have a piece.
We went into the observation deck by his study
And dispensed with formalities.

VALENTINA HART: Oh please go on!
You must go on!
Come on, girlfriend,
Spill, spill, spill, spill, spill!
Now go on,
Please go on.
Did Stewart let you see his art collection still?

TALIA BAILEY: His lips and mine locked in a kiss fantastic,
His hands roved freely 'neath my uniform,
I reached toward the presidential body,
And he got a call from the environmental conservation platform.
So I went on,
While he talked on the phone,
I took a position before him on my knees,
And I went on.
And he talked on.
Though what the Representative heard was
"Please, please, please, please, please!"
But then we didn't go on!

VALENTINA HART: You didn't go on?

TALIA BAILEY: No, he stopped me when he seemed upon the cusp.

VALENTINA HART: So you didn't go on?

TALIA BAILEY: No, we didn't go on.
He said he wasn't sure if I was someone he
Could
Trust.

[The lights fade as the girlfriends engage in cross talk.]

VALENTINA HART: Trust?

TALIA BAILEY: That's why we didn't go on.

VALENTINA HART: That's so weird! What did he think? That you'd go blabbin' this to the whole colony? Hey, what's that clicking?

TALIA BAILEY: I mean--rilly! Hey, what's that sound?

VALENTINA HART: It's just my gum synthesizer.

TALIA BAILEY: Oh--OK!

[As the relationship between Stewart and Talia continues, some members of the Presidential staff become worried about the prudence of continuing the relationship with so much potential for scandal. This song is a conversation between Zhang Walker, who, though worried, still thinks Talia is a good person, and the rather stonier SASHA HUNTER.]

"Time to Go"

ZHANG WALKER: They go back there,
They're just talking,
I'm sure she has a very thirsty mind.
She's interested in political philosophy and digital humanities.

SASHA HUNTER: I don't mind a girl who thinks,
It's just what else she does, methinks.
Zhang, it's Bailey's time to go.

ZHANG WALKER: She brings him
Little presents.
She really is a very thoughtful soul.
She even helped with peer review of his environmental conservation proposals.

SASHA HUNTER: It's not the gifts I mind as much
As her up real close and personal touch.
I tell ya, it's Miss Talia's time to go.

ZHANG WALKER: She never comes
When he's really busy.
Rarely is there anyone around.

SASHA HUNTER: Still the Security Force wears a frown.
They shouldn't worry, he checks her down.
But I'm not kidding, it's time for her to go.

ZHANG WALKER: Maybe she would like the Defense Ministry.

SASHA HUNTER: Good idea--don't wait!

ZHANG WALKER: Studly officers work at Defense Ministry.

SASHA HUNTER: Let's get Stewart's head on straight!

ZHANG WALKER: He comes back
From the Mars Colony Day ceremonies,
Soon she's bopping in the door.

SASHA HUNTER: "Glory to the Red Planet"
Shouldn't inspire thoughts so passionate.
Yes, it's really time for Talia to go.

[Time passes. Talia moves to the Defense Ministry in Fairview City, but the relationship intermittently continues. Meanwhile, a former aide named Sarah Chen sues the president for harassment, and it seems clear that before long, Stewart will have to testify under oath. Two close observers of those developments are old friends Valentina Hart and an operative named LUCIA GOLDMAN, who is friendly with lawyers for Chen and lawyers in the office of Independent Investigator KENNETH BARNES. One day, Hart and Goldman talk on the holophone.]

"Talk, Talk, Chat, Chat" (sprightly)

GOLDMAN and HART: Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old galpals swap the latest word.
Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old girlfriends dish the latest dirt.

GOLDMAN: I got tickets
To the space opera,
The store says I've got forty credits due,
I lost my appetite
At lunch on Thursday.
That's it for me,
Now tell me what's up with you.

HART: My friend Talia?
From the Presidential Dome?
I'm pretty sure what she's saying here is true.
It seems this Talia chick
Has been involved with the president's--

GOLDMAN: Oh that's sick!

HART: And the two of them are going to lie about it,
Too.

GOLDMAN: Back up, Valentina,
Did I hear you rightly?
Stewart got into an intern's life?
God, this news is manna, Val!
At last our political movement will finally have its strife!

HART: Oh, you're a dreamer Lucia!
There'll be headlines, then he'll pull off an
Escape.
He'll spin the story, he'll turn the tables--

GOLDMAN: Unless you get that airhead down on tape.

HART: What?

GOLDMAN: Unless you get that silly, vapid, trampy time bomb
Down on tape.

HART: Oh--one more thing...

GOLDMAN: What?

HART: There's a uniform...

GOLDMAN: Hold on, let me call Kenny.

[Independent Investigator Barnes uses Hart to detain Talia. A few days later, the news breaks across all colonies. On the advice of his friend Harry Thompson, Stewart flat-out lies to his wife, to his loyalists, and to the public about the relationship.]

"I Never Have" (performance should build in tempo and intensity)

STEWART: You know I'd like to answer questions,
An act my lawyers won't allow.
I'll give you more not less, sooner not later,
I just can't say a word right now.
But I don't know why she'd say these things
Her head's full of who knows what.
But I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that n--
Barnes has spent forty million credits,
There's desperation on his face.
An utter waste of public money,
An investigatorial disgrace.
All he's got is some recordings
Made by a vengeful snitch.
I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that b--
A vast conservative conspiracy
Is using her to beat on me.
They wanna torpedo my agenda
They hate me and my policies.
My work on environmental conservation and artistic expression funding.
But I will never let them ruin
Our dreams for a better world.
I tell ya, I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that
Girl.

[The presidential debate arrives. Stewart faces off against the opposition spokesman on the holo-broadcast. The exchange is heated.]

"The Great Debate" (rapid-fire, combative)

HAMILTON: The president's character is in question,
His moral failings plain to see.
Tonight the colonies witness his disgrace,
A turning point in history!

STEWART: You talk of character but offer nothing,
Your policies are empty air.
The colonies see through your moral posturing,
They know exactly what is there.

HAMILTON: The polls predicted we would dominate,
This debate would seal your fate.
Every analyst agreed with certainty,
Your downfall they did anticipate!

[The debate concludes. Commentators flood the holo-channels.]

COMMENTATOR [speaking]: The presidential debate went exactly as the analysts predicted. Hamilton's aggressive tactics resonated with conservative voters. Democrats are reeling tonight. The opposition emerged from this debate energized and united.

GOLDMAN [speaking to Hart afterward]: Did you see the debate? Hamilton crushed him. The predictions were spot-on—Stewart looked weak. Our movement is ascendant!

[Months of investigation, legal wrangling, and public relations campaigning follow. Barnes's tactics come under heavy fire, to which he responds.]

"Crossing the Line"

BARNES: It's true Talia asked to lawyer up,
Which Bittman put the lid on.
And I felt bad about her mother's grilling
Upon our little gridiron.
The Democrats and liberals
Blast these tactics of mine,
But a man's gotta do what a man's gotta do
When the president crosses the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
Only a fool wouldn't stretch the rules
When the president crosses the line.
It may have seemed like dirty pool
To drag his people 'fore the jury.
We wasted lots of Vernon's time,
May have busted Zhang Walker.
His aides aren't the innocent bystanders
As they claim when they moan and whine.
They won't say what they know full well:
The president crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
I'd be a nitwit not to bend a bit
When the president crosses the line.
The talking heads are accusing me
Of laying a perjury trap.
But all it catches is lying men.
Honest men beat the rap.
There's people who say I'm against love;
I've loved. It's fine.
But lying about it gets my blood up
And the president's crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
Tell Steve Brill I'll leak at will
When the president crosses the line.
This raises existential questions about leadership and applied ethics.

[After months of denials and futile delays, Stewart finally testifies before the Barnes grand jury and argues that, technically, he didn't lie.]

"Testimony" (snappy)

STEWART: Depends what the definition of "is" is,
Depends on the meaning of relations,
"Alone together" is literal nonsense,
Before you reach conclusions, read your documentation.
This is a matter of complexity science in language interpretation.

[Afterward, he speaks to the colonies, admits doing wrong, and apologizes, though grudgingly.]

STEWART: Inappropriate was the nature of our actions,
And believe me I regret the whole damn thing,
But inappropriate are all these personal questions,
The colonies don't need to know these things.
My work on environmental conservation should be the focus.

[Stewart's enemies reject his apology, and soon the Colonial House of Representatives begins the long process of impeachment. NATHAN HAMILTON here discloses his approach.]

"Bring 'em Down" (dark, moody)

HAMILTON: Mustn't seem to be too cheerful,
Mustn't overreach,
Must remember to seem unhappy
That we're going to impeach.
Must remember to remain sober
As we undertake this chore.
At the same time, let's remember
To pin some stuff on the Vice President.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Sure, they were elected,
Twice, in point of fact.
Voters obviously were bewildered
To have made a choice like that.
Now, like charging soldiers,
We'll move in for the sack.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Our political movement will finally succeed.
The debate showed we could defeat them,
The midterms will finish the job.
Every analyst predicts we'll dominate,
Conservative seats will grow by the mob.

[The House votes to hold impeachment hearings. The midterm elections are held in Richmond Town and across the colonies. Hamilton campaigns vigorously, confident in the forecasts. On election night, SARA LI and MOHAMMAD CRUZ watch the returns with Stewart.]

"Election Night" (tense, building)

SARA LI: The first results from Titan Station,
Democrats hold strong.

MOHAMMAD CRUZ: But surely that's an aberration,
The night is still young and long.

SARA LI: Now Mars returns are coming in,
We've picked up two new seats.

MOHAMMAD CRUZ: The outer colonies reporting,
Our candidates avoid defeats.

STEWART [speaking]: What's happening? Every pundit said we'd lose seats tonight. The opposition was supposed to gain ground—they were so certain after months of scandal coverage.

SARA LI: Earth's districts now declaring,
Democratic gains continue still.

MOHAMMAD CRUZ: The forecasters are bewildered,
Their models failed to fill the bill.

[Goldman watches from her apartment, stunned.]

GOLDMAN [speaking into holophone]: Lucia here. I'm seeing the results. This wasn't supposed to happen. After everything—the scandal, Barnes's investigation, months of coverage—the opposite outcome occurred. The voters didn't follow the script.

[Hamilton resigns as Speaker. The practical chances of Stewart's removal evaporate. As the show ends, we hear from Barnes, Bailey, and Stewart.]

"The People Have Spoken" (dramatic, stirring)

BARNES: The votes were cast and counted,
I can't believe what they had to say.
I had Stewart boxed into a corner
Looks like he's going to get away.
I spent four years and forty million
That's a lot of time and credits.
I made Stewart look ridiculous,
But the only scalp I got was Nathan's.
The experts were certain of our triumph,
Instead the Democrats gained ground.

TALIA BAILEY: The votes were cast and counted,
I can't believe what they had to say.
My boyfriend is still in office
And he might return to me one day.
You think perhaps that he will not want me
For all the trouble I've caused so far,
But he knows I can always make him happy
With my art and my passion for environmental conservation.
Maybe we can work together from Carmel, Estoria someday.

STEWART: The votes were cast and counted,
I can't believe what they had to say.
The removal threat is over,
Kenneth Barnes should go away.
I tell you, though, it is a mystery,
I mean, I'm unfaithful and I lie.
I might be guilty of obstruction,
Yet my ratings are sky-high.
The predictions said we'd suffer losses,
The forecasts all went wrong.
Instead my party emerged stronger,
Our coalition proved more strong.
That must mean I'm a pretty good president,
Though how, I don't think I know.
My work on environmental conservation and artistic expression funding resonates.
But obviously I'm not Barnes or Hamilton,
Which may be why they love me so.
Which may be why they love me so.

[Curtain.]
